messages:
elaine: Quick heads-up — we are running a BYOK incident sim tomorrow 09:00 PT with AcmeCorp. Goal: validate RBAC changes, audit log chain, and emergency key fallback. Who can own which piece?
raj: I can own RBAC + grants. Prep note: the bridge service account needs kms:Encrypt, kms:Decrypt, kms:CreateGrant on the CMK. Also restrict kms:CreateGrant to a narrow principal set.
tasha: I’ll take audit logging and retention. Compliance asked for immutable audit export for 365 days for this customer. We should test streaming logs to their SIEM and to our secure archive.
mike: I’ll run the incident play through (hand-off + break-glass). We should simulate key unavailability and ensure fallback to the cached model variant works without exposing plaintext to us.
ops-bot: Reminder: incident-sim-runbook template: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/byok-incident-sim (version 2026-03-12). Use /ops simulate-byo for automated checklist.
raj: Quick RBAC checklist draft:
```
- service-account: bridge-svc@redwood
  roles:
  - kms.Encrypt
  - kms.Decrypt
  - kms.CreateGrant (condition: request.from=bridge)
- group: ops-oncall
  roles: [kms.RewrapKey, kms.DisableKey]
- role: security-auditors
  permissions: [logs.Read, logs.Export]
```
Keep CreateGrant audited.
elaine: Good. For the sim we also need to validate the grant lifecycle: creation, use by inference runtime, and auto-expire/cleanup. Can we add a step to revoke stale grants?
raj: Yes — add a test that creates a short-lived grant (TTL 10m), performs an inference cycle, then we run a kill-switch to ensure Decrypt fails after TTL. If revoke fails, note as vuln.
tasha: On logs: two things to validate — 1) HSM event stream (key ops, import/export, wrap/unwrap) is captured with non-repudiable sigs; 2) KMS audit trail (grant create/revoke, key state transitions) is shipped to customer SIEM via signed delivery. We'll check checksums.
mike: Which compliance bar are we testing? Is this just AcmeCorp NAD (internal) or full-regulatory (PCI/HIPAA)?
elaine: Contract says SOC2 + HIPAA. So HIPAA-presence: ensure we never persist PHI in clear in logs; mask tokens/inputs in traces.
asha: (typo fix) tasha: Also add a step to validate key rotation path — import a rotated key and ensure old grants are invalidated.
raj: Vulnerability triage note: if we find a grant TTL mis-apply that allows extended decrypt, classify as high. We need a short RCA template for the sim: impact, root cause, mitigation, customer notification timeline.
ops-bot: Action created: #INC-2345 (incident-sim) assigned to mike, raj, tasha — due 1767320967.
security-bot: Compliance checklist appended to ticket: SOC2/CCPA/HIPAA items populated.
mike: For the break-glass test, propose steps:
1) disable-key on CMK (ops-oncall)
2) verify runtime falls back to cached key material (if allowed) OR fails gracefully with error 
3) confirm no secret leakage to logs
4) execute restore path (reenable, rewrap grants)

elaine: One more ask — RBAC change window: limit to 15 minutes and require two approvers (security + customer rep). We'll record approvals in the audit log (signed).
raj: I’ll prepare a minimal RBAC migration patch and post in #eng-releases for a quick review tonight. Will include tests for grant exhaustion and a repro script.
tasha: For log retention: set customer export to S3 with object lock for 365d. Also enable cross-account logging to their monitoring account.
mike: Plan sounds good. During the sim, if we observe any deviation from expected audit chain, we escalate to oncall and freeze further ops until RCA.
elaine: Perfect. Last ask: capture timeline and key snapshots (hashes) at each step. We need cryptographic evidence for the post-sim report.
raj: ACK. I’ll add a small script to produce key-hash snapshots and signed manifests.
elaine: Thanks all — I’ll send invite and runbook. Please add any blockers here. :thumbsup:
